correctness.rationale: Independent geometric discovery-stage decomposition shows a coupled first-repetition indicator representation for the same coupon sequence. Conditioning on a first repeated draw gives the exact shifted sum of geometric stages, including the terminal all-distinct branch, proving strict first-order stochastic order. Covariances with the indicators give the negative finite double sum for every n>=2. Gaussian survival bounds give first-two Rayleigh moments and dominated Riemann sums give the -sqrt(pi/8) residual covariance. An explicit independent completion-time coupling, together with the classical inclusion-exclusion Gumbel limit, gives independent weak limits. Variances give the stated scaled Pearson correlation. The standalone check separately compares rational formulas, complete prefix enumeration for n<=6, conditional means, and numerical asymptotic values; finite assertions are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The target is the bivariate law of first repeated coupon and complete collection on the same iid uniform sample path. The inspected classical work establishes marginal birthday times, coupon completion times, and discovery-stage representation, not the stated exact cross-covariance, conditional stochastic order, and residual covariance coefficient. Separate marginal statements do not imply joint dependence. Further priority risks remain from generalized two-stopping-time or coefficient-enumeration methods and a relevant unavailable full text.

value.rationale: First collision (birthday stopping time) and complete coverage are canonical, intrinsically coupled milestones in one sequence. The exact strict stochastic-order theorem is stronger than a covariance sign and determines the dependence for any nondecreasing test functions. The all-n covariance identity and its nonzero sqrt(n)-scale constant, alongside Rayleigh–Gumbel asymptotic independence and n-scaled correlation, isolate a natural second-order effect not inferable from the separate marginals. This is a motivated structural dependence statement, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
